properties.displayName: [WEEKLY] Internet-Exposed AI Agent/LLM Service Spawns Shell or LOLBin After Inbound Connection
properties.description:
Detects an interpreter-hosted AI/LLM/MCP service (python, uvicorn, gunicorn, node) that accepts an inbound connection from a public/non-loopback source and then spawns a Unix shell or LOLBin child within a short window — the post-auth-bypass remote-code-execution chain. This matters this fortnight because a cluster of critical advisories all describe unauthenticated reach into agent-execution or management surfaces that the same process then turns into command execution: PraisonAI's Jobs API and unauth MCP connect/SSE endpoints (GHSA-fq2m-6wqh-x44g, GHSA-p75f-6fp4-p57w, GHSA-x227-pf99-vffg), LiteLLM's Host-header auth bypass on management routes (CVE-2026-49468), googleapis/mcp-toolbox's opaque-token bypass (CVE-2026-11718), and @acastellon/auth's spoofable-header bypass (GHSA-gfj5-979r-92pw). The chain spans delivery (exposed 0.0.0.0 listener), exploit (missing/bypassed auth on a critical function), and execution (shell/LOLBin spawned by the service). It fires when the AI service process is the direct parent of an OS command interpreter shortly after a public inbound connection — the signature of agent-exec/command-injection RCE — and does NOT fire on local-loopback agent calls, on the service's own normal subprocess use that isn't a shell/LOLBin, or on shells spawned by non-AI parents. IOC slots (`<c2_domain_list>`, `<sha256_list>`) are placeholders for enrichment, not the detection logic.

Rationale: Every article in scope describes an unauthenticated path into an interpreter-hosted AI/LLM/MCP service that ends in command execution; correlating a public inbound connection to that service with the same process spawning a shell/LOLBin captures the shared exploit→execution chain rather than any one product's IOCs or endpoint paths.
properties.query:
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSeconds = 300;   // 300s = service-RCE spawn is near-immediate; >5m is almost always unrelated
let Inbound = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
    | where RemoteIPType == "Public"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python.exe","pythonw.exe","uvicorn","gunicorn","node","node.exe")
    | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("praison","litellm","mcp","uvicorn","fastapi","toolbox","aiui","agent")
    | project InboundTime = TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteIP, LocalPort, ServiceCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python.exe","pythonw.exe","uvicorn","gunicorn","node","node.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh","busybox","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl","curl.exe","wget","wget.exe","nc","ncat","socat","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","whoami","whoami.exe","id","chmod","base64")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| join kind=inner Inbound on DeviceId
| where TimeGenerated between (InboundTime .. InboundTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| project TimeGenerated, InboundTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, InboundTime), DeviceName, RemoteIP, LocalPort, AccountName, ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildProc = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
